title: Limit of an inverse system of complexes with ML terms and essentially constant H^{-1} (Stacks 070E)
statement:
For an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] $(B_i)_{i\ge1}$ of abelian groups (transition homomorphisms $B_{i+1}\to B_i$, hence composites $B_k\to B_i$ for $k\ge i$) let $\varprojlim_iB_i=\{(x_i)\in\prod_iB_i: x_{i+1}\mapsto x_i\}$. The system is *Mittag-Leffler* (ML) [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system] if for every $i$ there is $c(i)\ge i$ with $\operatorname{Im}(B_k\to B_i)=\operatorname{Im}(B_{c(i)}\to B_i)$ for all $k\ge c(i)$. It is *essentially constant* [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system] if there are an abelian group $X$ with homomorphisms $X\to B_i$ compatible with the transition maps, an index $i_0$ and a homomorphism $B_{i_0}\to X$ such that $X\to B_{i_0}\to X$ is the identity and for every $j$ there is $k\ge\max(i_0,j)$ such that $B_k\to B_j$ equals the composite $B_k\to B_{i_0}\to X\to B_j$.

Now let $(A^{-2}_i\xrightarrow{d^{-2}_i}A^{-1}_i\xrightarrow{d^{-1}_i}A^0_i\xrightarrow{d^0_i}A^1_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an inverse system of complexes of abelian groups ($d^{j+1}_id^j_i=0$; transition maps $A^j_{i+1}\to A^j_i$ commuting with the $d$'s), let $A^j=\varprojlim_iA^j_i$ with the induced complex $A^{-2}\to A^{-1}\to A^0\to A^1$, let $H^j_i=\ker d^j_i/\operatorname{im}d^{j-1}_i$ ($j=-1,0$) with the induced inverse systems, and let $H^{-1},H^0$ be the corresponding cohomology groups of the limit complex. If $(A^{-2}_i)$ and $(A^{-1}_i)$ are ML and $(H^{-1}_i)$ is essentially constant, then the canonical map $H^0\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$, $[(x_i)_i]\mapsto([x_i])_i$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Notation and the three short exact sequences of systems. For $j\in\{-2,-1,0\}$ and $i\ge1$ put $Z^j_i=\ker(d^j_i)\subseteq A^j_i$ and, for $j\in\{-1,0\}$, $I^j_i=\operatorname{im}(d^{j-1}_i)\subseteq A^j_i$; since $d^jd^{j-1}=0$, $I^j_i\subseteq Z^j_i$ and $H^j_i=Z^j_i/I^j_i$. The transition maps $A^j_{i+1}\to A^j_i$ commute with the differentials, so they map $Z^j_{i+1}$ into $Z^j_i$ and $I^j_{i+1}$ into $I^j_i$; thus $(Z^j_i)_i$, $(I^j_i)_i$ are inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system], the inclusions $(I^j_i)\to(Z^j_i)\to(A^j_i)$ and the maps $d^{j-1}_i:A^{j-1}_i\to I^j_i$ (corestriction) and $Z^j_i\to H^j_i$ are morphisms of inverse systems, and the induced transition maps of $(H^j_i)$ are those of the statement. Levelwise exactness gives the short exact sequences of inverse systems of abelian groups (exact at every $i$): (a) $0\to(Z^{-2}_i)\to(A^{-2}_i)\xrightarrow{d^{-2}}(I^{-1}_i)\to0$; (b) $0\to(Z^{-1}_i)\to(A^{-1}_i)\xrightarrow{d^{-1}}(I^0_i)\to0$; (c) $0\to(I^{-1}_i)\to(Z^{-1}_i)\to(H^{-1}_i)\to0$; (d) $0\to(I^0_i)\to(Z^0_i)\to(H^0_i)\to0$.

proof.text: Kernels commute with limits. In $A^0=\varprojlim_iA^0_i$ the kernel of $d^0=\varprojlim_id^0_i:A^0\to A^1$, $(x_i)\mapsto(d^0_i(x_i))$, is the set of compatible families $(x_i)$ with $d^0_i(x_i)=0$ for all $i$, i.e. $\ker(d^0)=\varprojlim_iZ^0_i$ (a compatible family of elements of the subgroups $Z^0_i$). Likewise $\varprojlim_iI^0_i\subseteq\varprojlim_iZ^0_i\subseteq A^0$ as subgroups (the maps on limits induced by the inclusions are injective, being inclusions of sets of families).

source.place: Homology, proof of Lemma 070E, lines 7829--7830 ('taking kernels commutes with limits')

proof.text: The image systems are ML. $(A^{-2}_i)$ and $(A^{-1}_i)$ are ML by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] (2) to the short exact sequences (a) and (b) of Step 1 (middle terms $(A^{-2}_i)$, $(A^{-1}_i)$), the quotient systems $(I^{-1}_i)$ and $(I^0_i)$ are ML.

$(Z^{-1}_i)$ is ML. In the short exact sequence (c) of Step 1, $(I^{-1}_i)$ is ML (Step 3) and $(H^{-1}_i)$ is essentially constant by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-sequence-ml] (the direction 'if the kernel system is ML then the middle system is ML'), $(Z^{-1}_i)$ is ML.

$\operatorname{im}(d^{-1})=\varprojlim_iI^0_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] (3) to the short exact sequence (b) of Step 1, whose kernel system $(Z^{-1}_i)$ is ML (Step 4): the map $\varprojlim_iA^{-1}_i\to\varprojlim_iI^0_i$, $(y_i)\mapsto(d^{-1}_i(y_i))$, is surjective. Composed with the inclusion $\varprojlim_iI^0_i\subseteq A^0$ of Step 2 this map is $d^{-1}=\varprojlim_id^{-1}_i:A^{-1}\to A^0$. Hence the image of $d^{-1}$ in $A^0$ is exactly the subgroup $\varprojlim_iI^0_i$.

The limit of (d) is short exact. For the short exact sequence (d) of Step 1, the sequence $0\to\varprojlim_iI^0_i\to\varprojlim_iZ^0_i\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-tower-limit-exact-surjective-kernels] (b), first assertion (with $R=\mathbf Z$: abelian groups are $\mathbf Z$-modules and homomorphisms are $\mathbf Z$-linear); since $(I^0_i)$ is ML (Step 3), $\varprojlim_iZ^0_i\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] (3). So $0\to\varprojlim_iI^0_i\to\varprojlim_iZ^0_i\xrightarrow{q}\varprojlim_iH^0_i\to0$ is exact, where $q((x_i)_i)=([x_i])_i$.

source.place: Homology, proof of Lemma 070E, lines 7849--7862 (Lemma 02N1 (1) and (3))

proof.text: Conclusion. By definition $H^0=\ker(d^0)/\operatorname{im}(d^{-1})$, which by Steps 2 and 5 is $\varprojlim_iZ^0_i/\varprojlim_iI^0_i$. By Step 6, $q$ induces an isomorphism $\varprojlim_iZ^0_i/\varprojlim_iI^0_i\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$, and this isomorphism sends the class of $(x_i)\in\ker(d^0)$ to $([x_i])_i$: it is the canonical map $H^0\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$ of the statement. Hence that map is an isomorphism.
